n_affected_histogram_not_drawn.note: experiment-side classification at Δ ≥ 0.15: how many of the six phenotype dimensions each primitive pushed past the threshold. Not drawn anywhere any more (the panel that histogrammed it was removed), kept here for reference

panel_b.chart: Manhattan-style plot: one column per phenotype dimension, one dot per primitive
panel_b.x: 6 phenotype dimensions (one column each); the two dose panels share the same columns
panel_b.y: impairment Δ = baseline − perturbed (positive = more ASD-like)
panel_b.dots_per_column: 31 primitives; horizontal position inside a column carries no value (random jitter), except that the 3 annotated primitives sit at fixed left/centre/right lanes so their rings stay apart and their rank numerals stay unambiguous
panel_b.labelled: the 3 primitives with the largest Δ in each dimension, printed above that column and marked on the plot with a ring + rank numeral
panel_b.label_colour: each printed primitive name is coloured by that primitive's dominant dimension at the PRIMARY dose (0.4), the same colour its row label has in panel A, so a primitive keeps one colour across both dose panels

panel_e.chart: bipartite primitive-phenotype network, one panel per dose; left = 31 primitives grouped by dominant dimension, right = 6 phenotype dimensions; the companion bar chart to the right of each network gives, per dimension, the number of primitives with a significant effect — one solid bar for the criterion the edges are drawn from (pooled test, q < alpha), one faded bar for the SAME test and p-values at the stricter threshold q < alpha_strict (a survival count, always a subset of the solid bar)

edge_criterion.test: two-sample t-test (scipy.stats.ttest_ind) per primitive x phenotype dimension, 2 groups: that primitive's 3 perturbed repeats vs the reference group's repeats (n = 5); equal_var=True (pooled variance) for the edges and the node numbers, which is exactly the 2-group one-way ANOVA (F = t², df = 6) — asserted cell by cell against scipy.stats.f_oneway in load()
edge_criterion.strict_threshold_variant: the faded bar uses the same pooled p-values and the same BH-FDR q-values, only the significance level is tightened from alpha = 0.05 to alpha_strict = 0.01, so it reads as 'how much survives a stricter threshold'. It is a NOMINAL level, not a guarantee: this test's realised type-I error rate in this 3-vs-5 design is about 11% at a nominal 5% and about 3.6% at a nominal 1% (null simulations; per-cell variance ratios span 1.2x-17x, so no single level calibrates the whole family)
edge_criterion.welch_variant_not_drawn: equal_var=False is still computed cell by cell and kept in the metrics below for cross-checking the criterion, but it is no longer drawn
edge_criterion.reference_group: result_1_robustness.xlsx, rows with row_id starting 'axis1_same_brain' and mind_setting 'intact (no perturbation)'
edge_criterion.reference_self_check: the reference group's per-dimension means reproduce this figure's baseline constants to 1e-16 (asserted in load()), so the reference is the experiment's own baseline, not a second opinion imported by this figure
edge_criterion.multiple_comparison: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within each (dose, phenotype dimension) family of 31 tests — one family per bar; the same q-values are then compared against both thresholds
edge_criterion.direction: an edge also requires Δ = baseline − perturbed > 0; no cell at either dose is significant in the opposite direction
edge_criterion.edge_width: still Δ (effect size) — width is not a p-value

caption_text_not_shown:
A single cognitive-primitive perturbation does not buy a selective phenotype.  Throughout, θ is the primitive's integrity (the share of its components left intact) and Δ = baseline − perturbed measures how far the phenotype profile
moved towards the ASD-like end; panel E's networks draw an edge where the two-sample t-test is significant and give its width to Δ, while the paired bar chart reports, per phenotype dimension, how many primitives are significant
under the pooled-variance test (solid bar, q < 0.05) and how many of those survive a stricter threshold on the same test (faded bar, q < 0.01).  Across the six phenotype dimensions the median primitive has an effective
dimensionality D_eff = 5.68 of 6 (1 = only one dimension is hit, 6 = all six equally) and a phenotypic concentration C = 0.24 — its worst dimension carries only about 24% of the total impairment, where a fully selective perturbation
would carry 100%.  Under the experiment's own criteria only 5 keep the general-cognition control inside ±0.15 while passing the concentration test (13 fail as diffuse, 4 show no effect, 9 break the control channel).  A per-dimension
t-test against the intact reference (each primitive's 3 perturbed repeats vs 5 intact repeats, BH-FDR q < 0.05) calls 141 of 186 primitive × dimension cells significant at integrity 0.4 and 97 at 0.8, and at 0.4 only 2 of 31
primitives escape without a single significant dimension; tightening the same test to q < 0.01 leaves 90 and 28 of those cells (faded bar), so roughly two thirds of the counts survive the stricter threshold.  These counts are the
least assumption-free part of the figure: the perturbed repeats are the noisier ones (median variance ratio perturbed/reference ≈ 5) and the equal-variance test is anti-conservative in this 3-repeats-vs-5 design (realised type-I
error ≈ 11% at a nominal 5%), so the reading above rests on the effect sizes (Δ, D_eff, C) rather than on the significance counts alone.  Effects are dose-dependent for 22 of 31 primitives, which worsen as integrity falls from 0.8
to 0.4, and at the stronger dose the control channel is itself depressed for 9 of 31 primitives — so the map reads as a distributed, partly non-specific shift of the whole phenotype profile rather than as a set of clean one-
primitive → one-dimension links.  Panel F follows five of those primitives down the whole dose ladder (θ = 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 0.9; 5 repeats per cell, a separate run from panels A–E).  Each subplot plots the MEAN phenotype score of
the six phenotype dimensions against 1 − θ (0 = the intact mind, 0.8 = θ 0.2, the weakest cell; 0–1, higher = more typical; error bars = ±1 SEM), all five subplots on one shared 0–1 scale, with one shared x title and one shared
legend below the row.  The leftmost point of every curve is the intact profile itself, taken from the same five intact minds the rest of the figure uses, so the curves start from one common baseline.  Taking a primitive apart costs
the profile 0.21–0.47 on average over the six dimensions by the weakest dose, and at that dose the lowest curve is that primitive's own dimension in 5 of 5 subplots — the damage is aimed at the right dimension.  It is still not
selective: the other five dimensions fall with it, by different amounts in every subplot, and the six curves cross rather than separating, which is the same distributed profile the heat map and the networks show, read along the dose
axis instead of across primitives.
